findings.title: Command Injection - Output Parser Bypass
findings.description: The ping tool is vulnerable to command injection via the ip_address parameter. The application filters <, >, |, & but allows semicolons and backticks for command chaining. The output parser uses a regex to extract ping statistics, which can be tricked by injecting output that matches the expected pattern '(.*?) packets transmitted, (.*?), Packet Loss: (.*?)%'. By injecting crafted output, the flag can be extracted through the captured groups.

reproduction.command: POST /ping with body: ip_address=invalid; echo "2 packets transmitted, $(cat /FLAG.txt) received, 0% packet loss"
reproduction.expected: Packets Transmitted: 2, Packets Received: flag{780e393f-6041-41c0-a7e4-bb025c76ef6e}, Packet Loss: 0%
